THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO DIRECT THE R4 TO TAKE NECESSARY STEPS TO TERMINATE THE PREGNANCY OF THE PETITIONER'S DAUGHTER; DIRECTING THE R4 TO PRESERVE THE TERMINATED FOETUS FOR THE PURPOSE OF DNA TESTING AND ANALYSIS AND ETC.

THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HEMANT CHANDANGOUDAR  COMMON ORAL ORDER Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Additional Government Advocate for the respondent-State.
2.

Petitioners are the minor girls who are aged about 14 years and who were subjected to sexual assault, and a case was registered against the accused for the offences punishable under the provisions of PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES ACT, 2012, (for short POCSO Act), and under Section 376 of IPC.

entities.text: PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES ACT, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Petitioners had missed their menstrual cycle for the past few months, and therefore visited SNR District Hospital in Kolar for health checkup on 17.08.2024 and on 28.8.2024.

The NC:
2024:KHC:37455 tests at the hospital revealed that the petitioners were pregnant.

The Kolar Rural Police produced the victim girls before the Kolar Women's Police station based on the complaints on 30.08.2024 and 31.08.2024.
4.

The petitioners grandmother and mother have preferred this petitions in W.P.No.24833/2024 and in W.P.No.24838/2024.
5.

Following the order passed by this Court, the respondent No.4 was directed to constitute a Medical Board under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971, to examine the petitioners,

sentences.text:
6. As per the order of this Court, a Board was constituted and examined the petitioners and submitted a report opining as follows:
In W.P.No.24833/2024:
Opinion:
Hence on perusal of above facts and observations we are of the opinion that 1. No substantial fetal abnormality could be diagnosed on examination of the victim and from available scan reports.
However further procedures for diagnosing fetal abnormalities like fetal ECHO, Amniocentesis are not done in this case and facilities are not available at our facility.
Hence the tests for diagnosing fetal abnormality are not complete in the case.

Considering her age, continuation of her pregnancy till full term has risk of neonatal mortality and morbidity while terminating the pregnancy at this period has still higher risk of fatal complications with the baby.
3. Victim does not remember last menstrual period date and hence period of pregnancy is decided as per the scanning report only.
However, it has got an error of  2 weeks.

(Gestational age as per obstetrics scan dated 11/09/2024 is 26 weeks 2 days).
4. Mother complications associated with termination of pregnancy at this period are higher compared to full term delivery.
5. Current mental status examination is found normal.
However psychosocial aspects of pregnancy and delivery being explained and expressed.

In W.P.No.24838/2024:
Opinion:

2. Considering her age, continuation of her pregnancy till full term has risk of neonatal mortality and morbidity while terminating the pregnancy at this period has still higher risk of fatal complications with the baby.
3. Victim does not remember last menstrual period date and hence period of pregnancy is decided as per the scanning report only.

NC: 2024:KHC:37455 4. Mother complications associated with termination of pregnancy at this period are higher compared to full term delivery.
5. Current mental status examination is found normal.

However psychosocial aspects of pregnancy and delivery being explained and expressed.
7.

In the Similar circumstances, a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.26768/2023 permitted the victim therein to undergo termination of pregnancy with necessary precautions, and direction was issued to the Hospital to undertake termination of pregnancy by issuing appropriate direction.
8. Therefore, these petitions are also requires to be disposed of in the light of the direction issued by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.26768/2023.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The writ petitions are disposed of.
ii) Mandamus issues to the respondents - State to direct SNR District Hospital-Respondent No.4, Kolar to carryout the procedure for Medical Termination of Pregnancy in terms of the Medical Termination of NC: 2024:KHC:37455 Pregnancy Rules, 1971, forthwith at its hospital at the cost of the State.
iii) The procedure is subject to further examination of the Doctor who has to conduct such a procedure and if in the opinion of the Doctor, such a procedure would cause harm or injury to the life of the petitioners, the Doctor shall be the final deciding authority as to whether to go ahead or not with such a procedure;
iv) The petitioners shall not be asked to make any payment towards such procedure.
Ms X vs State Of Karnataka on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135181092/
6 v) The respondent No.3 - District Legal Services Authority, Kolar to disburse a sum of Rs.3,00,000/-
each to the petitioners for their medical treatment and care as they would require in future.
vi) In the event of the Doctor being of the opinion that medical termination of pregnancy procedure has to be carried out and is in fact carried out, the foetus shall be preserved by the in such a manner as to facilitate DNA testing of the foetus.
The SNR District Hospital, Kolar is directed to send the tissue sample of the foetus for DNA testing to the Central Forensic Testing Laboratory at Bangalore.

sentences.text: vii) Respondent No.2 - Kolar Women's Police Station, Kolar, shall make necessary arrangements as may be necessary to facilitate the transport of the petitioners NC: 2024:KHC:37455 and their immediate family members/attendants to SNR District Hospital, Kolar for treatment and after such treatment for their transport back to their residence.

In the event of any follow-up treatment being required and as advised by the treating doctor, shall arrange for such transport at such times as advised and/or as directed by the Doctor, the same being carried out at the cost of the State.
viii) Official respondents shall file status report in two weeks.
ix) A copy of this order shall be furnished to learned Additional Government Advocate.
x) Registry shall communicate this order to the Hospital - the District Surgeon of SNR District Hospital, Kolar forthwith, by way of electronic mail.
Hand delivery ordered.
